title: Обещание Макса выиграть час  (Max Promises to Buy an Hour)

segments.t: Behind closed doors, Fedya weakly suggests the wedding guests might not remember the missing dishes, but Nagiyev roars that they paid a fortune for them and the bride is already in tears. When Chef Barinov says they need at least an hour, Max steps up and promises to stall the wedding party.
Шеф, у вас будет час, я все решу.
Я сам решаю, кто, куда, когда пошел.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Maybe they will not even remember those dishes?' The meaning hinges on 'maybe' working together with 'to remember' in spoken Russian.
'Shut your mouth, Fedya.' The grammar packs 'mouth' and 'Fedya' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Dmitry answers right away.
'They will remember every single thing.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'and' and finishing on 'to remember'.
'They paid good money for that menu.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'they', while 'pay' completes the thought.
'Cook it right now, fast.' The meaning hinges on 'quickly' working together with 'cook' in spoken Russian. Dmitry answers right away.
'Dima, we will not make it in time.' The grammar packs 'Dima' and 'we'll make it' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'We do not even have the ingredients here.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'by' and 'us' in a few short words.
Шеф, у вас будет час, я все решу.
'Chef, you will have your hour, I will handle everything.' Notice how Russian expresses 'chef' and 'I'll solve' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Dmitry answers right away.
'Get out of here right now.' In Russian, the idea of 'go' flows naturally into 'from here' without extra filler words.
Я сам решаю, кто, куда, когда пошел.
'I am the one who decides who goes where and when.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'I' before landing on 'go'.
'What did you just say, kid?' Fedya anchors the line on 'what', while 'baby' completes the thought. Dmitry answers right away.
'Did all of you hear that?' In Russian, the idea of 'did you hear?' flows naturally into 'yes' without extra filler words.
'Start prepping the appetizers, he will handle it.' The meaning hinges on 'cook' working together with 'will decide' in spoken Russian. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Шеф, у вас будет час, я все решу.
Я сам решаю, кто, куда, когда пошел.
